name: French bean
grown_as: A tender annual vegetable sown after frost: dwarf (bush) varieties 40 to 50 cm, and climbing varieties 2 m or more up canes. Flower colour (white, lilac or purple) and pod colour (green, yellow, purple) depend on the variety, which is not known: drawn as a dwarf bean with white flowers and green pods. ⚠️ CHECK
habit: Dwarf types: a bushy little plant 40 to 50 cm high. Climbing types: a slender stem twining round a cane anticlockwise, 2 to 3 m. Both slightly hairy, with leaves held well spaced on long stalks.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate (but the first pair of true leaves opposite)
leaf.leaflets: The middle leaflet on a longer stalk of its own (1 to 3 cm), symmetrical; the two side leaflets on short stalks and lopsided, the outer half wider. Tiny stipels at the base of each leaflet stalk.
leaf.outline: Each leaflet broadly oval to triangular-oval, 6 to 12 cm, widest below the middle
leaf.veins: A midrib and 4 to 6 curved side veins each side
leaf.surface: Thin, slightly rough with fine hairs, a little puckered
leaf.stalk: Long (5 to 15 cm), grooved, swollen at the base

flower.form: A small pea flower, the keel coiled into a tight spiral
flower.petals: Five: a broad standard, two wings spreading sideways and a spiral keel
flower.colour: White (in some varieties pale lilac or purple)
flower.behind: A small green cup-shaped calyx with two small bracts at its base
flower.carried: In short loose clusters of 2 to 8 on a stalk from the leaf joints, among or under the leaves

fruit: Slim pods 10 to 20 cm, round or slightly flat in section, smooth, green, ending in a thin curved beak, hanging in bunches from the leaf joints. Dry pods turn pale straw-buff and papery with the beans showing as bumps. Seed: a kidney-shaped bean 1 to 1.5 cm, its colour varying with variety (white, black, brown, mottled), with a small white scar on the inner curve.
seedling: The bean pushes up out of the soil as a hooked stem pulling up two thick, fleshy seed leaves (the bean's two halves). Between them opens the first pair of true leaves: simple, opposite, heart-shaped and pointed. Only after these do the three-leaflet leaves come.
winter: Nothing: killed by the first frost

leaf: three leaflets, the middle one on a longer stalk
each leaflet broad oval with a sharp pointed tip
bloom: a small pea flower with a coiled keel
seed: a small white scar on the inner curve
colour by variety: white, black, brown or mottled
seedling: two thick fleshy bean halves on the stem
a pair of opposite heart-shaped pointed simple leaves above them
young: a small bushy plant of three-leaflet leaves on long stalks
flower: small white pea flowers in loose clusters at the leaf joints
flowers partly hidden under the three-leaflet leaves
crop: slim smooth green pods hanging in bunches
seedhead: the beans showing as bumps through the pod
a thin beak at the end of each pod

look_alikes: Runner bean (Phaseolus coccineus) has bigger, rougher leaves, scarlet flowers in long spikes held clear of the leaves and coarse broad pods; its seed leaves stay underground. Broad bean has pinnate grey-green leaves.
